text:
mira: FWIW I ran a long-run with continuous batching + KV prefetch enabled and hit a steady memory climb. Repro steps and traces below. wondering if this is HOL blocking + fragments piling up

mike: can you paste the KV stats snapshot?

mira: sure — raw dump from /debug/kvcache right after 2h into the run:
```
KVCacheStats{
  total_entries: 1_328_471,
  fragments: 97,
  fragment_sizes: [64,128,256,4096],
  memory_bytes: 16_412_340_992,
  resident_pages: 125_231,
  page_faults: 8_421,
  evictions: 21_034,
  merges: 3_412,
  splits: 4_876,
  last_gc: 2026-03-10T18:04:12Z
}
```

mira: load profile: a mix of short chat requests (seq 64) and occasional long contexts (seq 32k) coming from the same user session. continuous batching merges small requests but occasionally attaches a long-context request into the same batch (we allow merge windows up to 50ms).

tara: long contexts will blow up the KV footprint for that batch because we materialize a huge KV range. Are we evicting eagerly after the batch finishes?

mira: eviction happens asynchronously. Evict logic tries to remove LRU fragments but fragmentation prevents big contiguous frees, so resident memory stays high. Also we see head-of-line blocking: while a batch needs pages, the worker holds the global kv lock and blocks other batches trying to make progress.

mike: do you have flame traces or pprof showing the HOL?

mira: yes — attached simplified stack sample (from pprof):
```
# top 8
2000  runtime/lock
1800  kvcache/page_read_sync
1700  runtime/block_on_futex
1500  serving/continuous_batcher/merge
1200  kvcache/evict_loop
```
```
# observation: page_read_sync spikes align with big-batch start times
```

tara: two orthogonal problems: 1) page reads are sync and hold the lock, 2) fragmentation means evict doesn't free enough contiguous address space.

mike: quick idea: make page read async and use a per-batch "wanted_pages" bitmap so we can release global lock while IO is in flight. Also limit merge when a candidate would introduce >N pages.

mira: I prototyped an async page read patch. Basic behavior improved: CPU waits went down and other batches progressed, but memory still grew because evict backlog couldn't compact fragments. Patch: defer_kv_prefetch = true (runtime flag)

mira: snippet of the experiment command:
```
./run_loadgen --mix profile.json --seq-mix "64:0.9,32000:0.1" --continuous-batch-window 50ms --kv-prefetch async --pprof kv_async.profile
```

kv-bot: CI: kv_async.profile uploaded to /artifacts/1771506789/kv_async.profile (size 12MB) :white_check_mark:

mike: good. For fragmentation we should try two things: compact-on-evict (coalesce adjacent fragments) and per-route namespacing so long-context batches don’t pollute the shared prefix cache. We already have route scoping in theory, maybe it's not applied during continuous merge.

tara: per-route scoping makes sense. Also consider a cap on "merge depth" — don't merge a long-context request into an existing short-batch. i.e. merge only if estimated_kv_pages(new_batch) + current_batch_pages < threshold.

mira: I added instrumentation for estimated_kv_pages. sample output mid-run:
```
BatchEstimate{batch_id: 3245, reqs: 18, est_kv_pages: 28}
BatchEstimate{batch_id: 3246, reqs: 3, est_kv_pages: 1800} # long context
```
mira: with threshold 1024 we prevented big merges. Memory growth rate dropped ~60% in the short test.

mike: nice. What's the perf/regression story? Did async prefetch regress latency tail?

mira: median latency unchanged, p99 improved for short requests because HOL reduced. Long ones see slightly higher p99 (they now pay IO without blocking others). Overall latency SLO improved for the mixed workload.

tara: are there any backend constraints? e.g. prefetch turned on by default for Hosted? We should gate the new behavior behind a config knob and do gradual rollouts.

mira: yes — plan: gate-by-route + runtime flag. Also start a background compaction job that runs when evictions > X/hr. Need to be careful with CPU cost.

mike: action items: 1) submit PR for async page read with unit tests (mira) 2) add merge-estimate threshold + config (mira + tara) 3) add compaction experiment (tara) 4) add feature flag and canary rollout plan (mike)

mira: I'll open the PRs today and attach test harness (loadgen scenarios). Expect initial canary to Dedicated customers only.

tara: Also add metrics: evict_fragment_count, compaction_runs, hol_block_seconds. We'll need dashboards.

mike: +1. Also add a debug endpoint to snapshot batch membership vs kv fragments so we can correlate which routes caused the fragmentation.

mira: noted. Will post PR links when ready. For repro: if anyone wants to reproduce locally: use the run_loadgen command above and set --kv-prefetch async or --kv-prefetch sync to compare.

ci-bot: created issue #INF-6312 "KV cache: async prefetch + merge threshold to reduce HOL and fragmentation" and assigned to @mira and @tara

mike: thanks everyone. Good to see actionable wins here. :rocket:
